messages:
maria_support: FYI customer ACME just escalated — getting intermittent 502s for streaming /v1/embeddings calls (hosted API). Started ~09:10 UTC, ~5% of requests failing. request-id sample: r-7f2c9
kevin_sre: digging in. which frontdoor stack? nginx or envoy? any recent deploys?
june_eng_runtime: Hosted frontdoor is NGINX for that region, midproxy (envoy) behind it. No infra deploys in last 2 hours.
oliver_support: I grabbed a failing trace from the customer: curl shows HTTP/1.1 502, body 'upstream prematurely closed connection'. They were streaming chunked with large X-Client-Meta header (~45KB).
maria_support: customer says it only fails when sending big metadata blobs with embeds; smaller requests are fine.
kevin_sre: preliminary hypothesis: header fragmentation/keepalive mismatch causing upstream to reset. Can someone paste the nginx error log around one example r-7f2c9?
june_eng_runtime: pasted from host nginx-frontend-3: "[error] 1024#0: *12345 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.4, server: hosted-api, request: \"POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1\", upstream: \"http://10.5.7.8:8080/\", host: \"api.redwood.ai\""
kevin_sre: Envoy logs show RST_STREAM from midproxy to runtime: "stream reset, error code: INTERNAL_ERROR" at same moments.
oliver_support: Repro steps I asked customer to try: curl -v -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' -H 'X-Client-Meta: <45KB base64>' -d @- https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
incidents-bot: New alert linked: edge-502-spike-1757777777 (severity: medium)
kevin_sre: Quick local repro attempt: reproduced 502 when header >32KB on nginx frontend. When I cap client_header_buffer_size to 4k, nginx splits header across buffers and then upstream gets half header — leads to mismatch and premature close.
june_eng_runtime: That matches. Runtime expects full header for tenant routing. If NGINX fragments and doesn't forward complete pseudo-headers before starting upstream connection, midproxy/hosted-runtime can error.
maria_support: Customer on a paid Dedicated plan; they're quite sensitive. What's a safe short-term mitigation we can propose?
kevin_sre: Short term: ask customer to shrink X-Client-Meta (workaround) or disable streaming chunking on their side for now. Operationally, we can bump nginx client_header_buffer_size/client_header_buffers on frontdoor and roll config to canary.
june_eng_runtime: I'll prepare a canary nginx config change: increase client_header_buffers from 4 16k to 8 32k and client_header_buffer_size 16k. Need SRE approval for canary on 10% of frontdoors.
oliver_support: Customer agreed to try non-streaming but prefers platform fix. They're available for a quick test once we roll canary.
kevin_sre: Plan: 1) quick canary bump to 10% frontdoors 2) monitor 502 rate, request-id correlate 3) if green, escalate rollout. I'll own the canary and rollback.
june_eng_runtime: Also adding an instrumentation: bad-header-size metric and increment when header_size > 32k to help correlate.
incidents-bot: Runbook reminder: for edge-502 patterns with header fragmentation, consider nginx header buffer config before touching runtime.
maria_support: Awesome. Please post the canary URL and TL;DR for the customer once canary is live.
kevin_sre: Canary deployed to fd-canary-2 at 09:42 UTC. Initial 10 minutes: 0.3% -> 0.05% 502 for ACME requests. Monitoring dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/d/edge/502-rate?panel=canary
june_eng_runtime: rolling instrumentation shows dropped header events dropped from 12/min -> 1/min on canary.
oliver_support: ACME just confirmed a successful streaming request with 46KB meta after we flipped them to canary. They report ~normal latency. :white_check_mark:
maria_support: Marking as customer-validated. Moving to postmortem doc and change request for global rollout. Thanks team.
kevin_sre: Follow-ups: add nginx config to infra repo, schedule full rollout during low traffic window, and add an automated alert when dropped-header > 1% of requests.
june_eng_runtime: Filing PR now: infra/nginx/frontdoor-config#472 (increase header buffers).
maria_support: Closing loop with ACME and sending credit offer for outage window.
kevin_sre: Closing incident in 30m if no regression.
incidents-bot: Incident closed (auto) at 09:55 UTC - resolved in canary, rollout scheduled.
